# **Assignment 06: Multimodal Search System for E-Commerce**

## **1\. Introduction**

An e-commerce search system should accept different forms of customer input while maintaining a consistent retrieval process. A customer may type a keyword, speak a product description, or provide a product image. This project designs and implements a small prototype that connects requirements analysis, three-layer architecture, UML modeling, and executable Python code, as specified in Assignment 06\.

The central design principle is:

**Different Inputs \-\> Common Query Representation \-\> Retrieval \-\> Ranking \-\> Results**

The required implementation supports text, simulated voice, and image-similarity search. It uses a local dataset of ten products, ten sample images, and three orders. The purpose is to demonstrate a coherent software design rather than a production shopping platform. Optional extensions include text-and-image fusion, filtering, stock-aware scoring, and order lookup.

## **2\. Problem Description**

The Customer searches a catalog containing shoes, bags, headphones, and watches. Product results include relevance scores and prices. Order queries return an order identifier, customer identifier, date, status, and total.

**Table 1\. Supported input modalities**

| Mode | Input | Processing | Output |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Text | Keywords or a natural-language sentence | Normalize text, retrieve matching products, rank candidates | Ranked products and scores |
| Voice | A supplied transcript representing speech-to-text output | Validate transcript, construct a voice query, reuse text retrieval | Ranked products and scores |
| Image | A local product-image file | Encode image, compare vectors using cosine similarity, rank candidates | Visually similar products and scores |
| Multimodal extension | Text and an image | Combine text and image scores | Ranked products with both score components |
| Order extension | Order ID or latest-order request | Look up order data | Order information or an explicit no-result message |

The console voice mode explicitly simulates speech-to-text. The website can request microphone input through a compatible browser's Web Speech API and submits the resulting transcript. The image pipeline processes actual sample files using lightweight color and spatial features by default.

Functional requirements describe observable operations of the system. The first seven requirements cover the core prototype; the remaining requirements cover the implemented extensions.

| ID | Requirement |
| :---- | :---- |
| FR01 | The system shall search products using keywords or natural-language text. |

| FR03 | The system shall search for products similar to an input product image. |
| FR04 | The system shall convert supported inputs into a common query representation. |
| FR05 | The system shall retrieve candidate products before ranking them. |
| FR06 | The system shall rank retrieved products and return the highest-scoring results first. |
| FR07 | The system shall display returned product information and ranking scores. |
| FR08 | The system shall search orders by order ID and display the corresponding information. |
| FR09 | The system shall find the latest order for a specified customer. |
| FR10 | The system shall support maximum-price, color, and category filters. |
| FR11 | The system shall combine text and image relevance in a multimodal query. |

### ***3.3 Non-Functional Requirements***

Non-functional requirements describe quality expectations. These expectations are proposed for the prototype; they are not additional thresholds specified by the assignment handout.

**Table 4\. Non-functional requirements**

| ID | Requirement |
| :---- | :---- |
| NFR01 | The prototype should return results within an acceptable time for a small local dataset. |
| NFR02 | The interface should present inputs, processing descriptions, returned products, and scores in a readable and consistent format. |
| NFR03 | The implementation should separate presentation, application, and data responsibilities to support maintenance. |
| NFR04 | Speech and image processing should be replaceable without changing the presentation interface. |
| NFR05 | Invalid input should produce a clear error instead of a misleading search result. |
| NFR06 | Repeated searches with unchanged inputs and data should produce deterministic results. |
| NFR07 | Search operations should be independently verifiable through automated tests. |

NFR01 is a qualitative target; a hardware-specific latency benchmark has not been claimed. NFR03 and NFR04 are assessed by reviewing dependencies and service boundaries. NFR06 and NFR07 are assessed through the supplied automated tests.

## **5\. Three-Layer Architecture**

### ***5.1 Layer Responsibilities***

**Table 9\. Responsibilities and implementation mapping**

| Layer | Responsibility | Python location |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Presentation | Accept command-line input and display search results | main.py and presentation/search\_ui.py |
| Application / Intelligence | Construct queries, process modalities, retrieve candidates, rank results | application/ |
| Data | Load product and order records; store and compare image vectors | data\_access/ and dataset/ |

The composition root, app\_factory.py, constructs and connects dependencies. Shared data objects reside in domain/. SearchUI does not read JSON files or access repositories.

### ***5.2 Component/Package Diagram***

**Figure 2\. Three-layer architecture**  
![][image2]

VoiceInput, ImageUpload, and SearchResultView are separate presentation classes used by SearchUI. SearchUI calls ImageService directly to encode an uploaded image, attaches the returned vector to the common query object, and submits the query to SearchService. SearchService accesses VectorIndex and ProductRepository, then calls RankingService. OrderService accesses OrderRepository. ImageStorage holds local PNGs; ImageService reads those files during encoding. The composition root builds catalog vectors before constructing VectorIndex. ProductDatabase and OrderDatabase are logical stores implemented with JSON, rather than database-server products.

### ***5.3 Component Responsibilities***

**Table 10\. Component responsibilities**

| Component | Responsibility |
| :---- | :---- |
| SearchUI | Collect input and coordinate application-service calls |
| QueryService | Normalize text and construct a common query object |
| SpeechService | Validate and return the simulated transcript |
| ImageService | Encode image files into feature vectors |
| SearchService | Retrieve candidates and apply filters |
| RankingService | Calculate final scores and sort candidates |
| ProductRepository | Read and expose product records |
| OrderService | Interpret order requests and call OrderRepository |
| OrderRepository | Find orders by ID or latest customer date |
| VectorIndex | Store product vectors and calculate cosine similarities |

### ***7.3 Query Service***

QueryService produces a QueryRepresentation for every modality. Text processing lowercases input, normalizes characters, tokenizes words, and removes a small set of stop words. Known color and category terms become filters. A phrase such as under 110 dollars becomes a maximum-price constraint.

query \= query\_service.text\_query("black running shoes")  
voice\_query \= query\_service.voice\_query("find running shoes")  
image\_query \= query\_service.image\_query(image\_path)

### ***7.4 Text Search***

SearchService compares descriptive query words with the product name, category, color, and description. Color, category, brand, and maximum price are first extracted as constraints. A candidate must satisfy every extracted constraint and every remaining descriptive word. A filter-only query can return all eligible products, ordered by business score.

text\_score \= matched query words / total unique query words

This implementation follows the handout's simple keyword-matching approach while normalizing the score for fusion. Constraint words and numbers are excluded from the text denominator. Thus "nike shoes under 100 dollars" correctly returns no product in this catalog; Adidas shoes do not satisfy the Nike brand constraint.

### ***7.5 Simulated Voice Search***

class SpeechService:  
    def transcribe(self, audio\_input: str) \-\> str:  
        if not audio\_input.strip():  
            raise ValueError("The simulated voice transcript cannot be empty.")  
        return audio\_input.strip()

In the console, the input is already a transcript. In the web interface, a compatible browser can capture speech using its Web Speech API and place the recognized transcript in the form. The Python server still receives text, so browser speech recognition quality is outside this evaluation.

### ***7.6 Image-Similarity Search***

The assignment permits artificial vectors for a first prototype. This implementation instead extracts simple features from real PNG files: 24 histogram values, comprising eight bins per RGB channel, and 27 spatial values, comprising mean RGB values for nine grid cells. The resulting 51-dimensional vector is normalized using its L2 norm.

cosine\_similarity(a, b) \= dot(a, b) / (norm(a) \* norm(b))

A zero denominator produces a similarity of zero. VectorIndex compares the query vector with every catalog vector. ImageService performs feature extraction; VectorIndex stores and compares vectors without importing application services.

### ***7.7 Result Ranking***

Retrieval identifies candidates; RankingService calculates their final order. The core relevance score is text similarity for text/voice and cosine similarity for image search.

business\_score \= 0.7 \* popularity \+ 0.3 \* min(stock / 20, 1\)  
final\_score \= 0.98 \* relevance \+ 0.02 \* business\_score

The business contribution is an optional extension. It has a small weight but can reorder sufficiently close relevance scores; it is not strictly limited to exact ties. Results are sorted by descending final score, then product ID for deterministic tie resolution. The default output contains up to five products.

## **8\. Multimodal Search Method**

Supporting three separate modalities is required. Combining text and image in a single query is an implemented extension. The fusion method preserves separate feature spaces and combines scores after retrieval.

**Figure 5\. Multimodal processing flow**

![][image6]

multimodal\_relevance \= 0.5 \* text\_score \+ 0.5 \* image\_score

Both weights sum to one, following the handout's fusion example. The combined relevance is then passed to the same final ranking formula used by individual modalities. Text-derived filters apply before final ranking.

## **9\. Experimental Results**

### ***9.1 Demonstration of Required Queries***

**Table 14\. Demonstration inputs, processing, and outputs**

| Mode | Input | Processing | Top returned product | Final score |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | ----: |
| Text | black running shoes | Normalize; filter; retrieve; rank | Nike Black Running Shoes | 0.9963 |
| Voice | find running shoes under 110 dollars | Simulated transcription; normalize; filter; retrieve; rank | Adidas White Running Shoes | 0.9971 |
| Image | nike\_black\_running\_shoes.png | Encode; cosine retrieval; rank | Nike Black Running Shoes | 0.9963 |
| Multimodal | black shoes \+ Nike sample image | Text/image retrieval; fusion; rank | Nike Black Running Shoes | 0.9963 |

The image query obtains a cosine similarity of 1.000 for its identical catalog image. The final score is slightly lower because it also includes business information.

The current console demonstration can be reproduced with `python main.py demo` inside `code/`. It prints each input, a processing summary, returned products, and ranking scores. The web evidence below shows the same search service through the browser interface.

**Table 15\. Top-1 evaluation**

| ID | Query | Mode | Expected Top-1 | Actual Top-1 | Success |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| E01 | black running shoes | Text | Nike Black Running Shoes | Nike Black Running Shoes | Yes |
| E02 | running shoes under 110 dollars | Text | Adidas White Running Shoes | Adidas White Running Shoes | Yes |
| E03 | find blue sports shoes | Voice | Blue Sports Shoes | Blue Sports Shoes | Yes |
| E04 | find black headphones | Voice | Black Wireless Headphones | Black Wireless Headphones | Yes |
| E05 | black\_leather\_bag.png | Image | Black Leather Bag | Black Leather Bag | Yes |
| E06 | green\_sports\_watch.png | Image | Green Sports Watch | Green Sports Watch | Yes |
| E07 | black shoes \+ sample image | Multimodal | Nike Black Running Shoes | Nike Black Running Shoes | Yes |
| E08 | nike shoes under 100 dollars | Text | No result | No result | Yes |
| E09 | black shoe | Text | Nike Black Running Shoes | Nike Black Running Shoes | Yes |
| E10 | order O001 | Order | O001 | O001 | Yes |

Success Rate \= Successful Queries / Total Queries  
             \= 10 / 10  
             \= 100.00%

**Table 16\. Evaluation summary**

| Measure | Result |
| :---- | :---- |
| Number of queries | 10 |
| Successful queries | 10 |
| Success rate | 100.00% |
| Incorrect Top-1 examples in this test set | None |
| Evaluation scope | Controlled local dataset; image queries reuse catalog images; one negative text case and one order case |

These results measure controlled retrieval consistency, not general image recognition or production accuracy. The image demonstration returns Brown Travel Bag among the shoe query's Top-5 results, illustrating a visually misleading lower-ranked result even though the Top-1 test succeeds.

### ***10.2 Strengths and Limitations***

**Table 19\. Discussion of design choices**

| Aspect | Strength | Limitation |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Architecture | Responsibilities and retrieval/ranking stages are separated | A local prototype rather than a deployed service |
| Voice | Reuses text processing; browser microphone can fill the transcript | Browser speech support varies and is not measured |
| Text | Transparent scoring and basic filters | Substring matching; limited language understanding |
| Image | Actual image files and repeatable vectors | Color and layout features can confuse unrelated products |
| Fusion | Score contributions can be inspected | Equal weights are chosen manually |
| Evaluation | Reproducible expected Top-1 results | Small test set and repeated catalog images |
| Orders | ID and latest-order lookup are demonstrated | No authentication or customer-access enforcement |

The optional web interface is implemented in Flask. Optional environment settings enable pretrained MobileNet image embeddings (`SEARCH_IMAGE_ENCODER=mobilenet`), SQLite vector storage (`SEARCH_VECTOR_BACKEND=sqlite`), and latent semantic text embeddings (`SEARCH_TEXT_MODE=semantic`). These modes were smoke tested separately. SQLite stores vectors persistently but performs exact scans, not approximate nearest-neighbor indexing. The latent semantic mode is trained on only ten products and can return weakly related items. Browser speech recognition requires a compatible browser and permission. Price, category, stock-aware ranking, order lookup, and multimodal fusion are also implemented.

## **11\. Conclusion**

The prototype implements the three required product-search modes and demonstrates their relationship to a three-layer software design. Text and simulated voice queries use keyword retrieval, image queries use vector similarity, and a shared query envelope supports consistent orchestration. Candidate retrieval and ranking remain separate. Ten product records and ten sample images support the demonstration, while thirteen automated tests and ten evaluation queries provide reproducible evidence.

The report includes the required actor, functional and non-functional requirements, use cases, architecture, voice-search sequence, implementation explanation, multimodal method, experimental results, and discussion. Optional fusion, filtering, business scoring, order search, browser interface, and configurable advanced retrieval modes extend the basic prototype. The Visual Paradigm project is supplied separately by the student.
